    Models¶

    The seven analysis methods are peers — sibling equinox.Module classes with no inheritance between them, each owning exactly the assumptions its math requires. Pick by problem structure: a single analysis time with a linear observation operator wants OI or 3DVar; an assimilation window with perfect-model dynamics wants strong-constraint 4DVar; admitting model error turns that into weak-constraint 4DVar; the operational linearise-and-iterate formulation with control-variable transform is incremental 4DVar; and replacing the inner-loop optimiser with a trained ConvLSTM gives 4DVarNet.

    Every model exposes .as_analysis_step(), returning a lightweight wrapper that satisfies the pipekit-cycle AnalysisStep Protocol — that is the seam through which all seven plug into VarDACycle / VarSmootherCycle interchangeably.

    Classical methods¶

    Closed-form and optimisation-based analyses. OptimalInterpolation is the linear-Gaussian BLUE solution and refuses non-linear observation operators at construction; ThreeDVar minimises the same cost iteratively and accepts non-linear operators; the three 4DVar variants extend the cost over a time window. IncrementalConfig collects the outer/inner-loop knobs of IncrementalFourDVar.

    vardax — Modular variational data assimilation with learned components.

    All public symbols are re-exported from the private _src subpackage so that user code imports from the top-level namespace:

    import vardax

model = vardax.FourDVarNet1D(...)

    class OptimalInterpolation(eqx.Module):
    r"""BLUE / OI — closed-form linear-Gaussian analysis.

    Attributes:
        obs_op: Observation operator. Must be linear (its
            ``linearize(x)`` must return an operator independent of
            ``x``). Use [`ThreeDVar`][vardax.ThreeDVar] for non-linear
            ``H``.
        prior_mean: Background $x_b$ of shape ``(T, N)``.
        prior_cov_op: Background-error covariance $B$ as a
            ``lineax.AbstractLinearOperator``.
        obs_cov_op: Observation-error covariance $R$ as a
            ``lineax.AbstractLinearOperator``.
        cg_atol: CG absolute tolerance for the inner solve.
        cg_rtol: CG relative tolerance for the inner solve.
        cg_max_steps: CG iteration cap.

    Examples:
        With $B = R = I$, identity $H$ and everything observed, the
        analysis splits the innovation in half: $x^* = y / 2$.

        >>> import jax, jax.numpy as jnp, lineax as lx, vardax
        >>> eye = lx.IdentityLinearOperator(jax.ShapeDtypeStruct((1, 3), jnp.float32))
        >>> oi = vardax.OptimalInterpolation(
        ...     obs_op=vardax.MaskedIdentity(),
        ...     prior_mean=jnp.zeros((1, 3)),
        ...     prior_cov_op=eye,
        ...     obs_cov_op=eye,
        ... )
        >>> batch = vardax.Batch1D(input=jnp.ones((1, 1, 3)), mask=jnp.ones((1, 1, 3)))
        >>> xa = oi(batch)
        >>> xa.shape
        (1, 1, 3)
        >>> bool(jnp.allclose(xa, 0.5, atol=1e-4))
        True
    """

    obs_op: Any  # ObservationOperator (linear)
    prior_mean: Float[Array, "T N"]
    prior_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator
    obs_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator
    cg_atol: float = eqx.field(static=True, default=1e-6)
    cg_rtol: float = eqx.field(static=True, default=1e-6)
    cg_max_steps: int = eqx.field(static=True, default=200)

    def __call__(self, batch: Batch1D) -> Float[Array, "B T N"]:
        """BLUE analysis for each sample in the batch."""

        def _one(
            input_i: Float[Array, "T N"], mask_i: Float[Array, "T N"]
        ) -> Float[Array, "T N"]:
            return self._analyse(
                self.prior_mean, input_i, mask_i, self.obs_op, self.obs_cov_op
            )

        return jax.vmap(_one)(batch.input, batch.mask)

    def _analyse(
        self,
        x_b: Float[Array, "T N"],
        input_i: Float[Array, "T N"],
        mask_i: Float[Array, "T N"],
        obs_op: Any,
        obs_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator,
    ) -> Float[Array, "T N"]:
        """BLUE analysis of one sample around the background ``x_b``."""

        # The effective observation operator is mask ⊙ H(·) — apply the
        # mask both to the predicted obs (innovation) AND to the
        # tangent-linear used to assemble (H B H^T + R). Without the
        # mask in `linearize`, missing entries are treated as
        # zero-innovation observations and bias the analysis whenever
        # B couples observed and missing components.
        def masked_obs(x: Float[Array, "T N"]) -> Float[Array, "T N"]:
            raw = obs_op(x, mask=mask_i) if _accepts_mask(obs_op) else obs_op(x)
            return mask_i * raw

        y_pred = masked_obs(x_b)
        innovation = (input_i * mask_i) - y_pred

        # Build (H B H^T + R) as a composed lineax operator. We
        # tag it positive-semidefinite so lineax.CG accepts it
        # (the composition itself doesn't carry the tag).
        H = lx.JacobianLinearOperator(lambda x, _args=None: masked_obs(x), x_b)
        inner_raw = H @ self.prior_cov_op @ H.transpose() + obs_cov_op
        inner_op = lx.TaggedLinearOperator(inner_raw, lx.positive_semidefinite_tag)

        solver = lx.CG(
            atol=self.cg_atol,
            rtol=self.cg_rtol,
            max_steps=self.cg_max_steps,
        )
        v = lx.linear_solve(inner_op, innovation, solver=solver).value

        # x_star = x_b + B H^T v
        return x_b + self.prior_cov_op.mv(H.transpose().mv(v))

    def as_analysis_step(self) -> _OIAnalysisStep:
        """Adapt to ``pipekit_cycle.AnalysisStep`` (Decision D8)."""
        return _OIAnalysisStep(self)

    ThreeDVar ¶

    Bases: Module

    3D variational analysis.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    obs_op Any

    Observation operator (linear or nonlinear).
    prior_mean Float[Array, 'T N']

    Background \(x_b\) of shape (T, N).
    prior_cov_op AbstractLinearOperator

    \(B\). lineax.AbstractLinearOperator.
    obs_cov_op AbstractLinearOperator

    \(R\). lineax.AbstractLinearOperator.
    minimiser AbstractMinimiser | Minimiser

    optimistix.AbstractMinimiser for the inner iteration (default optimistix.BFGS(rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-6)), or a Minimiser such as OptaxMinimiser.
    minimiser_adjoint AbstractAdjoint

    optimistix.AbstractAdjoint for differentiating through the minimum (used only if the ThreeDVar analysis is itself nested inside a larger training loop). Default ImplicitAdjoint — exact at the optimum.
    max_steps int

    Iteration cap on the inner solver when minimiser is an optimistix solver; a vardax Minimiser keeps its own.
    parameterization StateParameterization | None

    Optional StateParameterization. When given, the control is \(\theta\), the state is \(\psi(\theta)\) (reshaped to prior_mean.shape) and \(\mathrm{pen}(\theta)\) replaces the background term, so prior_mean and prior_cov_op are not used — nor is the forecast of the analysis-step adapter. Default None: the control is the state itself.

    Examples:

    With \(B = R = I\), identity \(H\) and everything observed, the analysis agrees with the closed-form BLUE, \(x^* = y / 2\).

    >>> import jax, jax.numpy as jnp, lineax as lx, vardax
>>> eye = lx.IdentityLinearOperator(jax.ShapeDtypeStruct((1, 3), jnp.float32))
>>> three = vardax.ThreeDVar(
...     obs_op=vardax.MaskedIdentity(),
...     prior_mean=jnp.zeros((1, 3)),
...     prior_cov_op=eye,
...     obs_cov_op=eye,
... )
>>> batch = vardax.Batch1D(input=jnp.ones((1, 1, 3)), mask=jnp.ones((1, 1, 3)))
>>> xa = three(batch)
>>> xa.shape
(1, 1, 3)
>>> bool(jnp.allclose(xa, 0.5, atol=1e-3))
True

    class ThreeDVar(eqx.Module):
    r"""3D variational analysis.

    Attributes:
        obs_op: Observation operator (linear or nonlinear).
        prior_mean: Background $x_b$ of shape ``(T, N)``.
        prior_cov_op: $B$. ``lineax.AbstractLinearOperator``.
        obs_cov_op: $R$. ``lineax.AbstractLinearOperator``.
        minimiser: ``optimistix.AbstractMinimiser`` for the inner
            iteration (default ``optimistix.BFGS(rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-6)``),
            or a [`Minimiser`][vardax.Minimiser] such as
            [`OptaxMinimiser`][vardax.OptaxMinimiser].
        minimiser_adjoint: ``optimistix.AbstractAdjoint`` for
            differentiating *through* the minimum (used only if the
            ``ThreeDVar`` analysis is itself nested inside a larger
            training loop). Default ``ImplicitAdjoint`` — exact at the
            optimum.
        max_steps: Iteration cap on the inner solver when ``minimiser``
            is an ``optimistix`` solver; a vardax `Minimiser` keeps its own.
        parameterization: Optional
            [`StateParameterization`][vardax.StateParameterization]. When
            given, the control is $\theta$, the state is
            $\psi(\theta)$ (reshaped to ``prior_mean.shape``) and
            $\mathrm{pen}(\theta)$ replaces the background term, so
            ``prior_mean`` and ``prior_cov_op`` are not used — nor is the
            ``forecast`` of the analysis-step adapter. Default ``None``:
            the control is the state itself.

    Examples:
        With $B = R = I$, identity $H$ and everything observed, the
        analysis agrees with the closed-form BLUE, $x^* = y / 2$.

        >>> import jax, jax.numpy as jnp, lineax as lx, vardax
        >>> eye = lx.IdentityLinearOperator(jax.ShapeDtypeStruct((1, 3), jnp.float32))
        >>> three = vardax.ThreeDVar(
        ...     obs_op=vardax.MaskedIdentity(),
        ...     prior_mean=jnp.zeros((1, 3)),
        ...     prior_cov_op=eye,
        ...     obs_cov_op=eye,
        ... )
        >>> batch = vardax.Batch1D(input=jnp.ones((1, 1, 3)), mask=jnp.ones((1, 1, 3)))
        >>> xa = three(batch)
        >>> xa.shape
        (1, 1, 3)
        >>> bool(jnp.allclose(xa, 0.5, atol=1e-3))
        True
    """

    obs_op: Any
    prior_mean: Float[Array, "T N"]
    prior_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator
    obs_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator
    minimiser: optx.AbstractMinimiser | Minimiser = eqx.field(static=True)
    minimiser_adjoint: optx.AbstractAdjoint = eqx.field(static=True)
    max_steps: int = eqx.field(static=True, default=200)
    parameterization: StateParameterization | None = None

    def __init__(
        self,
        obs_op: Any,
        prior_mean: Float[Array, "T N"],
        prior_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator,
        obs_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator,
        minimiser: optx.AbstractMinimiser | Minimiser | None = None,
        minimiser_adjoint: optx.AbstractAdjoint | None = None,
        max_steps: int = 200,
        parameterization: StateParameterization | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.obs_op = obs_op
        self.prior_mean = prior_mean
        self.prior_cov_op = prior_cov_op
        self.obs_cov_op = obs_cov_op
        self.minimiser = minimiser or optx.BFGS(rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-6)
        self.minimiser_adjoint = minimiser_adjoint or optx.ImplicitAdjoint()
        self.max_steps = max_steps
        self.parameterization = parameterization

    def __call__(self, batch: Batch1D | PointObsBatch) -> Float[Array, "B T N"]:
        r"""3DVar analysis for each sample in the batch.

        A [`PointObsBatch`][vardax.PointObsBatch] needs a point operator as
        ``obs_op``: a [`GridPointObs`][vardax.GridPointObs] on the state
        ``(T, N)`` (``time_index`` selects the row), or a
        [`FieldPointObs`][vardax.FieldPointObs] with a
        [`NeuralFieldParameterization`][vardax.NeuralFieldParameterization],
        which evaluates the field at the coordinates directly. The error
        variances are the batch's $\sigma_i^2$; ``obs_cov_op`` must be
        ``None`` or an identity (``ValueError`` otherwise).
        """
        if isinstance(batch, PointObsBatch):
            check_point_obs_cov(self.obs_cov_op)
            return map_point_batch(
                lambda b: self._analyse_points(self.prior_mean, b), batch
            )

        def _one(
            input_i: Float[Array, "T N"], mask_i: Float[Array, "T N"]
        ) -> Float[Array, "T N"]:
            return self._analyse(
                self.prior_mean, input_i, mask_i, self.obs_op, self.obs_cov_op
            )

        return jax.vmap(_one)(batch.input, batch.mask)

    def _analyse(
        self,
        x_b: Float[Array, "T N"],
        input_i: Float[Array, "T N"],
        mask_i: Float[Array, "T N"],
        obs_op: Any,
        obs_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator,
    ) -> Float[Array, "T N"]:
        """Minimise the 3D-Var cost of one sample around the background ``x_b``."""

        def obs_cost(x: Float[Array, "T N"]) -> Float[Array, ""]:
            # Observation term — apply R^{-1} via lineax solve.
            # Mask predictions AND observations symmetrically: for
            # obs_ops that don't take a `mask` kwarg (e.g.
            # LinearObs), unmasked predictions at missing entries
            # would otherwise penalise the analysis there.
            y_pred = obs_op(x, mask=mask_i) if _accepts_mask(obs_op) else obs_op(x)
            residual = mask_i * (input_i - y_pred)
            R_inv_r = lx.linear_solve(
                obs_cov_op,
                residual,
                solver=lx.CG(atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-6),
            ).value
            return 0.5 * jnp.sum(residual * R_inv_r)

        return self._solve(x_b, obs_cost)

    def _analyse_points(
        self, x_b: Float[Array, "T N"], batch: PointObsBatch
    ) -> Float[Array, "T N"]:
        """Minimise the 3D-Var cost of one point-observation sample."""
        if isinstance(self.obs_op, FieldPointObs):
            param = self.parameterization
            if not isinstance(param, NeuralFieldParameterization):
                raise TypeError(
                    "FieldPointObs evaluates a field: it needs "
                    "parameterization=NeuralFieldParameterization(...)."
                )
            field_op = self.obs_op

            def control_obs_cost(theta: Any) -> Float[Array, ""]:
                return point_obs_cost(field_op(param.as_field(theta), batch), batch)

            return self._solve(x_b, None, control_obs_cost=control_obs_cost)

        def obs_cost(x: Float[Array, "T N"]) -> Float[Array, ""]:
            return grid_point_obs_cost(self.obs_op, x, batch)

        return self._solve(x_b, obs_cost)

    def _solve(
        self,
        x_b: Float[Array, "T N"],
        obs_cost: Callable[[Array], Array] | None,
        *,
        control_obs_cost: Callable[[Any], Array] | None = None,
    ) -> Float[Array, "T N"]:
        """Minimise background (or penalty) plus ``obs_cost`` from ``x_b``."""
        param = self.parameterization
        if param is not None:
            # J(θ) = pen(θ) + J_o(ψ(θ)): the penalty replaces the B term.
            def decode(theta: Any) -> Float[Array, "T N"]:
                return param.decode(theta).reshape(x_b.shape)

            def param_cost(theta: Any, _args: Any) -> Float[Array, ""]:
                if control_obs_cost is not None:
                    return param.penalty(theta) + control_obs_cost(theta)
                assert obs_cost is not None
                return param.penalty(theta) + obs_cost(decode(theta))

            theta_star = minimise(
                self.minimiser,
                param_cost,
                param.init_control(),
                adjoint=self.minimiser_adjoint,
                max_steps=self.max_steps,
            )
            return decode(theta_star)

        def cost(x: Float[Array, "T N"], _args: Any) -> Float[Array, ""]:
            # Background term — apply B^{-1} via lineax solve.
            dx = x - x_b
            B_inv_dx = lx.linear_solve(
                self.prior_cov_op,
                dx,
                solver=lx.CG(atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-6),
            ).value
            j_bg = 0.5 * jnp.sum(dx * B_inv_dx)
            assert obs_cost is not None
            return j_bg + obs_cost(x)

        x_star = minimise(
            self.minimiser,
            cost,
            x_b,
            adjoint=self.minimiser_adjoint,
            max_steps=self.max_steps,
        )
        return x_star

    def as_analysis_step(self) -> _ThreeDVarAnalysisStep:
        """Adapt to ``pipekit_cycle.AnalysisStep`` (Decision D8)."""
        return _ThreeDVarAnalysisStep(self)

    StrongFourDVar ¶

    Bases: Module

    Strong-constraint 4DVar.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    forward Any

    pipekit_cycle.ForwardModel supplying step(state, dt) -> state.

    class StrongFourDVar(eqx.Module):
    r"""Strong-constraint 4DVar.

    Attributes:
        forward: ``pipekit_cycle.ForwardModel`` supplying
            ``step(state, dt) -> state``.
        obs_op: Observation operator.
        prior_mean: Background $x_b$ — initial state of shape
            ``(N,)`` (state vector at $t=0$).
        prior_cov_op: $B$.
        obs_cov_op: $R$.
        minimiser: ``optimistix.AbstractMinimiser`` for the outer
            optimisation over $x_0$ (default ``optx.BFGS(rtol=1e-6,
            atol=1e-6)``), or a [`Minimiser`][vardax.Minimiser] such as
            [`OptaxMinimiser`][vardax.OptaxMinimiser] for a large control.
        minimiser_adjoint: ``optimistix.AbstractAdjoint`` for
            differentiating through the minimum.
        forward_adjoint: ``diffrax.AbstractAdjoint``-like — currently
            stored as a tag, threaded through if the forward delegates
            to ``diffrax``. Default ``None`` (use forward's own).
        max_steps: Iteration cap on the outer solver when ``minimiser``
            is an ``optimistix`` solver; a vardax `Minimiser` keeps its own.
        parameterization: Optional
            [`StateParameterization`][vardax.StateParameterization]. When
            given, the control is $\theta$, $x_0 = \psi(\theta)$ (reshaped
            to ``prior_mean.shape``) and $\mathrm{pen}(\theta)$ replaces
            the background term, so ``prior_mean`` and ``prior_cov_op``
            are not used. Default ``None``: the control is $x_0$.

    Examples:
        Trivial dynamics ($M_t(x) = x$) and a single timestep reduce
        strong 4DVar to 3DVar, so with $B = R = I$ the analysis is
        $x_0^* = y / 2$.

        >>> import jax, jax.numpy as jnp, lineax as lx, vardax
        >>> class Identity:
        ...     dt = 1.0
        ...
        ...     def step(self, x, dt):
        ...         return x
        >>> eye = lx.IdentityLinearOperator(jax.ShapeDtypeStruct((3,), jnp.float32))
        >>> strong = vardax.StrongFourDVar(
        ...     forward=Identity(),
        ...     obs_op=vardax.MaskedIdentity(),
        ...     prior_mean=jnp.zeros(3),
        ...     prior_cov_op=eye,
        ...     obs_cov_op=eye,
        ... )
        >>> batch = vardax.Batch1D(input=jnp.ones((1, 1, 3)), mask=jnp.ones((1, 1, 3)))
        >>> strong(batch).shape
        (1, 3)
    """

    forward: Any
    obs_op: Any
    prior_mean: Float[Array, N]  # ty:ignore[unresolved-reference]
    prior_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator
    obs_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator
    minimiser: optx.AbstractMinimiser | Minimiser = eqx.field(static=True)
    minimiser_adjoint: optx.AbstractAdjoint = eqx.field(static=True)
    forward_adjoint: Any = eqx.field(static=True)
    max_steps: int = eqx.field(static=True, default=200)
    parameterization: StateParameterization | None = None

    def __init__(
        self,
        forward: Any,
        obs_op: Any,
        prior_mean: Float[Array, N],  # ty:ignore[unresolved-reference]
        prior_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator,
        obs_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator,
        minimiser: optx.AbstractMinimiser | Minimiser | None = None,
        minimiser_adjoint: optx.AbstractAdjoint | None = None,
        forward_adjoint: Any = None,
        max_steps: int = 200,
        parameterization: StateParameterization | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.forward = forward
        self.obs_op = obs_op
        self.prior_mean = prior_mean
        self.prior_cov_op = prior_cov_op
        self.obs_cov_op = obs_cov_op
        self.minimiser = minimiser or optx.BFGS(rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-6)
        self.minimiser_adjoint = minimiser_adjoint or optx.ImplicitAdjoint()
        self.forward_adjoint = forward_adjoint
        self.max_steps = max_steps
        self.parameterization = parameterization

    def _rollout(self, x_0: Float[Array, N], n_steps: int) -> Float[Array, "T N"]:  # ty:ignore[unresolved-reference]
        """Step the forward model ``n_steps`` times, returning the trajectory."""
        dt = self.forward.dt

        def step_fn(
            x: Float[Array, N],  # ty:ignore[unresolved-reference]
            _: None,
        ) -> tuple[Float[Array, N], Float[Array, N]]:  # ty:ignore[unresolved-reference]
            x_new = self.forward.step(x, dt)
            return x_new, x_new

        _, trajectory = jax.lax.scan(step_fn, x_0, None, length=n_steps)
        # Prepend x_0 so the trajectory has length T+1.
        return jnp.concatenate([x_0[None, :], trajectory], axis=0)

    def __call__(self, batch: Batch1D | PointObsBatch) -> Float[Array, "B N"]:
        """Strong-4DVar analysis: minimise over $x_0$.

        A [`PointObsBatch`][vardax.PointObsBatch] needs
        ``obs_op=GridPointObs(...)``: observation $i$ is compared with the
        trajectory state $x_{\tau_i}$, $\tau_i$ = ``time_index[i]``, over a
        window of ``n_times`` states, with error variance $\\sigma_i^2$
        (``obs_cov_op`` must be ``None`` or an identity,
        else ``ValueError``).
        """
        if isinstance(batch, PointObsBatch):
            check_point_obs_cov(self.obs_cov_op)
            n_steps = window_steps(batch)

            def _one_points(b: PointObsBatch) -> Float[Array, N]:  # ty:ignore[unresolved-reference]
                def obs_cost(x_0: Float[Array, N]) -> Float[Array, ""]:  # ty:ignore[unresolved-reference]
                    trajectory = self._rollout(x_0, n_steps=n_steps)
                    return grid_point_obs_cost(self.obs_op, trajectory, b)

                return self._solve(obs_cost)

            return map_point_batch(_one_points, batch)

        T = batch.input.shape[1] - 1  # rollout steps (input has T+1 timesteps)

        def _one(
            input_i: Float[Array, "T_plus_1 N"], mask_i: Float[Array, "T_plus_1 N"]
        ) -> Float[Array, N]:  # ty:ignore[unresolved-reference]
            def obs_cost(x_0: Float[Array, N]) -> Float[Array, ""]:  # ty:ignore[unresolved-reference]
                # Roll out the trajectory.
                trajectory = self._rollout(x_0, n_steps=T)

                # Observation term, summed across time.
                def _per_step(x_t, y_t, m_t):
                    y_pred = (
                        self.obs_op(x_t, mask=m_t)
                        if _accepts_mask(self.obs_op)
                        else self.obs_op(x_t)
                    )
                    residual = m_t * (y_t - y_pred)
                    R_inv_r = lx.linear_solve(
                        self.obs_cov_op,
                        residual,
                        solver=lx.CG(atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-6),
                    ).value
                    return 0.5 * jnp.sum(residual * R_inv_r)

                per_step_costs = jax.vmap(_per_step)(trajectory, input_i, mask_i)
                return jnp.sum(per_step_costs)

            return self._solve(obs_cost)

        return jax.vmap(_one)(batch.input, batch.mask)

    def _solve(
        self,
        obs_cost: Callable[[Array], Array],
    ) -> Float[Array, N]:  # ty:ignore[unresolved-reference]
        """Minimise background (or penalty) plus ``obs_cost(x_0)``."""
        param = self.parameterization
        if param is not None:
            # x_0 = ψ(θ); J(θ) = pen(θ) + J_o(M(ψ(θ))).
            def decode(theta: Any) -> Float[Array, N]:  # ty:ignore[unresolved-reference]
                return param.decode(theta).reshape(self.prior_mean.shape)

            def param_cost(theta: Any, _args: Any) -> Float[Array, ""]:
                return param.penalty(theta) + obs_cost(decode(theta))

            theta_star = minimise(
                self.minimiser,
                param_cost,
                param.init_control(),
                adjoint=self.minimiser_adjoint,
                max_steps=self.max_steps,
            )
            return decode(theta_star)

        def cost(x_0: Float[Array, N], _args: Any) -> Float[Array, ""]:  # ty:ignore[unresolved-reference]
            # Background term
            dx = x_0 - self.prior_mean
            B_inv_dx = lx.linear_solve(
                self.prior_cov_op,
                dx,
                solver=lx.CG(atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-6),
            ).value
            j_bg = 0.5 * jnp.sum(dx * B_inv_dx)
            return j_bg + obs_cost(x_0)

        return minimise(
            self.minimiser,
            cost,
            self.prior_mean,
            adjoint=self.minimiser_adjoint,
            max_steps=self.max_steps,
        )

    def as_analysis_step(self) -> _StrongFourDVarAnalysisStep:
        return _StrongFourDVarAnalysisStep(self)

    class WeakFourDVar(eqx.Module):
    r"""Weak-constraint 4DVar with augmented control vector.

    Attributes:
        forward: ``pipekit_cycle.ForwardModel`` (the free model
            $M_t^\text{free}$).
        obs_op: Observation operator.
        prior_mean: Background $x_b$ — initial state ``(N,)``.
        prior_cov_op: $B$.
        obs_cov_op: $R$.
        model_err_cov_op: $Q$ — covariance of the per-step model
            error $\eta_t$. Defaults to identity scaled by a
            small variance if not supplied (effectively
            strong-constraint with a tiny relaxation).
        minimiser: As in [`StrongFourDVar`][vardax.StrongFourDVar].
        minimiser_adjoint: As in [`StrongFourDVar`][vardax.StrongFourDVar].
        max_steps: As in [`StrongFourDVar`][vardax.StrongFourDVar].
        parameterization: Optional
            [`StateParameterization`][vardax.StateParameterization] of the
            initial state. When given, the control is $(\theta, \eta)$,
            $x_0 = \psi(\theta)$ and $\mathrm{pen}(\theta)$ replaces the
            background term (``prior_mean`` and ``prior_cov_op`` are not
            used). Default ``None``: the control is $(x_0, \eta)$.

    Examples:
        Trivial dynamics and a single timestep: no model-error steps
        remain ($T = 0$) and the analysis initial state reduces to the
        3DVar / BLUE answer $x_0^* = y / 2$ for $B = R = I$.

        >>> import jax, jax.numpy as jnp, lineax as lx, vardax
        >>> class Identity:
        ...     dt = 1.0
        ...
        ...     def step(self, x, dt):
        ...         return x
        >>> eye = lx.IdentityLinearOperator(jax.ShapeDtypeStruct((3,), jnp.float32))
        >>> weak = vardax.WeakFourDVar(
        ...     forward=Identity(),
        ...     obs_op=vardax.MaskedIdentity(),
        ...     prior_mean=jnp.zeros(3),
        ...     prior_cov_op=eye,
        ...     obs_cov_op=eye,
        ...     model_err_cov_op=eye,
        ... )
        >>> batch = vardax.Batch1D(input=jnp.ones((1, 1, 3)), mask=jnp.ones((1, 1, 3)))
        >>> x0_star, eta_star = weak(batch)
        >>> x0_star.shape, eta_star.shape
        ((1, 3), (1, 0, 3))
    """

    forward: Any
    obs_op: Any
    prior_mean: Float[Array, N]  # ty:ignore[unresolved-reference]
    prior_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator
    obs_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator
    model_err_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator
    minimiser: optx.AbstractMinimiser | Minimiser = eqx.field(static=True)
    minimiser_adjoint: optx.AbstractAdjoint = eqx.field(static=True)
    max_steps: int = eqx.field(static=True, default=200)
    parameterization: StateParameterization | None = None

    def __init__(
        self,
        forward: Any,
        obs_op: Any,
        prior_mean: Float[Array, N],  # ty:ignore[unresolved-reference]
        prior_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator,
        obs_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator,
        model_err_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator,
        minimiser: optx.AbstractMinimiser | Minimiser | None = None,
        minimiser_adjoint: optx.AbstractAdjoint | None = None,
        max_steps: int = 200,
        parameterization: StateParameterization | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.forward = forward
        self.obs_op = obs_op
        self.prior_mean = prior_mean
        self.prior_cov_op = prior_cov_op
        self.obs_cov_op = obs_cov_op
        self.model_err_cov_op = model_err_cov_op
        self.minimiser = minimiser or optx.BFGS(rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-6)
        self.minimiser_adjoint = minimiser_adjoint or optx.ImplicitAdjoint()
        self.max_steps = max_steps
        self.parameterization = parameterization

    def _rollout_with_error(
        self,
        x_0: Float[Array, N],  # ty:ignore[unresolved-reference]
        etas: Float[Array, "T N"],
    ) -> Float[Array, "T_plus_1 N"]:
        r"""Roll out with per-step model error.

        Each step applies $x_t = M_t^\text{free}(x_{t-1}) + \eta_t$.
        """
        dt = self.forward.dt

        def step_fn(
            x: Float[Array, N],  # ty:ignore[unresolved-reference]
            eta_t: Float[Array, N],  # ty:ignore[unresolved-reference]
        ) -> tuple[Float[Array, N], Float[Array, N]]:  # ty:ignore[unresolved-reference]
            x_new = self.forward.step(x, dt) + eta_t
            return x_new, x_new

        _, trajectory = jax.lax.scan(step_fn, x_0, etas)
        return jnp.concatenate([x_0[None, :], trajectory], axis=0)

    def __call__(
        self,
        batch: Batch1D | PointObsBatch,
    ) -> tuple[Float[Array, "B N"], Float[Array, "B T N"]]:
        """Weak-4DVar analysis.

        Returns ``(x_0_star, eta_star)`` — the analysis initial state
        and the per-step model-error trajectory (one row per
        timestep, total ``T``).

        A [`PointObsBatch`][vardax.PointObsBatch] needs
        ``obs_op=GridPointObs(...)``: observation $i$ is compared with the
        trajectory state at ``time_index[i]`` over a window of ``n_times``
        states (so ``T = n_times - 1``), with error variance
        $\\sigma_i^2$ (``obs_cov_op`` must be ``None`` or an identity,
        else ``ValueError``).
        """
        N = self.prior_mean.shape[0]
        if isinstance(batch, PointObsBatch):
            check_point_obs_cov(self.obs_cov_op)
            n_steps = window_steps(batch)

            def _one_points(b: PointObsBatch):
                def traj_obs_cost(
                    trajectory: Float[Array, "T_plus_1 N"],
                ) -> Float[Array, ""]:
                    return grid_point_obs_cost(self.obs_op, trajectory, b)

                return self._solve(traj_obs_cost, n_steps, N)

            return map_point_batch(_one_points, batch)

        # T_plus_1 timesteps in the batch ⇒ T model-error steps.
        T_plus_1 = batch.input.shape[1]
        T = T_plus_1 - 1
        N = batch.input.shape[2]

        def _one(
            input_i: Float[Array, "T_plus_1 N"], mask_i: Float[Array, "T_plus_1 N"]
        ):
            def traj_obs_cost(
                trajectory: Float[Array, "T_plus_1 N"],
            ) -> Float[Array, ""]:
                def _per_step(x_t, y_t, m_t):
                    y_pred = (
                        self.obs_op(x_t, mask=m_t)
                        if _accepts_mask(self.obs_op)
                        else self.obs_op(x_t)
                    )
                    residual = m_t * (y_t - y_pred)
                    R_inv_r = lx.linear_solve(
                        self.obs_cov_op,
                        residual,
                        solver=lx.CG(atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-6),
                    ).value
                    return 0.5 * jnp.sum(residual * R_inv_r)

                per_step_costs = jax.vmap(_per_step)(trajectory, input_i, mask_i)
                return jnp.sum(per_step_costs)

            return self._solve(traj_obs_cost, T, N)

        x0_star, eta_star = jax.vmap(_one)(batch.input, batch.mask)
        return x0_star, eta_star

    def _solve(
        self,
        traj_obs_cost: Callable[[Array], Array],
        T: int,
        N: int,
    ) -> tuple[Float[Array, " N"], Float[Array, "T N"]]:
        """Minimise over $(x_0, \\eta)$ (or $(\\theta, \\eta)$) for one sample."""

        def model_and_obs_cost(
            x_0: Float[Array, " N"],
            etas: Float[Array, "T N"],
        ) -> Float[Array, ""]:
            # Model-error term
            def _eta_cost(eta_t):
                Q_inv_eta = lx.linear_solve(
                    self.model_err_cov_op,
                    eta_t,
                    solver=lx.CG(atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-6),
                ).value
                return 0.5 * jnp.sum(eta_t * Q_inv_eta)

            # A one-state window has no model-error steps (vmap over an
            # empty axis would trip lineax's CG on a zero-size operand).
            j_eta = (
                jnp.sum(jax.vmap(_eta_cost)(etas))
                if etas.shape[0] > 0
                else jnp.zeros((), dtype=x_0.dtype)
            )

            # Observation term
            j_obs = traj_obs_cost(self._rollout_with_error(x_0, etas))
            return j_obs + j_eta

        # Initial guess: x_0 at the background, etas at zero.
        init_etas = jnp.zeros((T, N))

        param = self.parameterization
        if param is not None:
            # Control (θ, η); x_0 = ψ(θ) and pen(θ) replaces the B term.
            def decode(theta: Any) -> Float[Array, " N"]:
                return param.decode(theta).reshape(self.prior_mean.shape)

            def param_cost(control: Any, _args: Any) -> Float[Array, ""]:
                theta, etas = control
                return param.penalty(theta) + model_and_obs_cost(decode(theta), etas)

            theta_star, eta_star = minimise(
                self.minimiser,
                param_cost,
                (param.init_control(), init_etas),
                adjoint=self.minimiser_adjoint,
                max_steps=self.max_steps,
            )
            return decode(theta_star), eta_star

        def cost(control: Float[Array, "T_plus_1 N"], _args: Any) -> Float[Array, ""]:
            x_0 = control[0]
            etas = control[1:]

            # Background term
            dx = x_0 - self.prior_mean
            B_inv_dx = lx.linear_solve(
                self.prior_cov_op,
                dx,
                solver=lx.CG(atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-6),
            ).value
            j_bg = 0.5 * jnp.sum(dx * B_inv_dx)
            return j_bg + model_and_obs_cost(x_0, etas)

        y0 = jnp.concatenate([self.prior_mean[None, :], init_etas], axis=0)

        control_star = minimise(
            self.minimiser,
            cost,
            y0,
            adjoint=self.minimiser_adjoint,
            max_steps=self.max_steps,
        )
        return control_star[0], control_star[1:]

    def as_analysis_step(self) -> _WeakFourDVarAnalysisStep:
        return _WeakFourDVarAnalysisStep(self)

    class IncrementalFourDVar(eqx.Module):
    r"""Operational incremental 4DVar (Decision D11).

    Functionally equivalent to [`StrongFourDVar`][vardax.StrongFourDVar]
    (same problem, same answer in the converged limit) but with a
    specialised inner solver: Gauss-Newton outer iterations and CG
    inner iterations on the linearised cost. Use this for production /
    long-window 4DVar.

    Attributes:
        forward: ``pipekit_cycle.ForwardModel``.
        obs_op: Observation operator.
        prior_mean: Background $x_b$ — initial state ``(N,)``.
        prior_cov_op: $B$.
        obs_cov_op: $R$.
        config: [`IncrementalConfig`][vardax.IncrementalConfig].

    Examples:
        Trivial dynamics ($M_t(x) = x$) and a single timestep reduce
        the problem to 3DVar, so with $B = R = I$ the converged
        analysis is $x_0^* = y / 2$.

        >>> import jax, jax.numpy as jnp, lineax as lx, vardax
        >>> class Identity:
        ...     dt = 1.0
        ...
        ...     def step(self, x, dt):
        ...         return x
        >>> eye = lx.IdentityLinearOperator(jax.ShapeDtypeStruct((3,), jnp.float32))
        >>> inc = vardax.IncrementalFourDVar(
        ...     forward=Identity(),
        ...     obs_op=vardax.MaskedIdentity(),
        ...     prior_mean=jnp.zeros(3),
        ...     prior_cov_op=eye,
        ...     obs_cov_op=eye,
        ... )
        >>> batch = vardax.Batch1D(input=jnp.ones((1, 1, 3)), mask=jnp.ones((1, 1, 3)))
        >>> xa = inc(batch)
        >>> xa.shape
        (1, 3)
        >>> bool(jnp.allclose(xa, 0.5, atol=1e-2))
        True
    """

    forward: Any
    obs_op: Any
    prior_mean: Float[Array, N]  # ty:ignore[unresolved-reference]
    prior_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator
    obs_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator
    config: IncrementalConfig

    def __init__(
        self,
        forward: Any,
        obs_op: Any,
        prior_mean: Float[Array, N],  # ty:ignore[unresolved-reference]
        prior_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator,
        obs_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator,
        config: IncrementalConfig | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.forward = forward
        self.obs_op = obs_op
        self.prior_mean = prior_mean
        self.prior_cov_op = prior_cov_op
        self.obs_cov_op = obs_cov_op
        self.config = config or IncrementalConfig()

    def _rollout(
        self,
        x_0: Float[Array, N],  # ty:ignore[unresolved-reference]
        n_steps: int,
    ) -> Float[Array, "T_plus_1 N"]:
        dt = self.forward.dt

        def step_fn(x, _):
            x_new = self.forward.step(x, dt)
            return x_new, x_new

        _, trajectory = jax.lax.scan(step_fn, x_0, None, length=n_steps)
        return jnp.concatenate([x_0[None, :], trajectory], axis=0)

    def __call__(self, batch: Batch1D | PointObsBatch) -> Float[Array, "B N"]:
        """Incremental-4DVar analysis: GN outer + CG inner.

        A [`PointObsBatch`][vardax.PointObsBatch] needs
        ``obs_op=GridPointObs(...)``: observation $i$ is compared with the
        trajectory state at ``time_index[i]`` over a window of ``n_times``
        states, with error variance $\\sigma_i^2$ (``obs_cov_op`` must
        be ``None`` or an identity, else ``ValueError``).
        """
        if isinstance(batch, PointObsBatch):
            check_point_obs_cov(self.obs_cov_op)
            n_steps = window_steps(batch)
            return map_point_batch(lambda b: self._analyse_points(b, n_steps), batch)

        T = batch.input.shape[1] - 1

        def _one(input_i, mask_i):
            x_b = self.prior_mean

            def cost_grad_for_outer(x_iter):
                """Gradient of the full nonlinear cost at ``x_iter``."""

                def cost_full(x_0):
                    dx = x_0 - self.prior_mean
                    B_inv_dx = lx.linear_solve(
                        self.prior_cov_op,
                        dx,
                        solver=lx.CG(atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-6),
                    ).value
                    j_bg = 0.5 * jnp.sum(dx * B_inv_dx)
                    trajectory = self._rollout(x_0, n_steps=T)

                    def _per_step(x_t, y_t, m_t):
                        y_pred = (
                            self.obs_op(x_t, mask=m_t)
                            if _accepts_mask(self.obs_op)
                            else self.obs_op(x_t)
                        )
                        residual = m_t * (y_t - y_pred)
                        R_inv_r = lx.linear_solve(
                            self.obs_cov_op,
                            residual,
                            solver=lx.CG(atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-6),
                        ).value
                        return 0.5 * jnp.sum(residual * R_inv_r)

                    per_step = jax.vmap(_per_step)(trajectory, input_i, mask_i)
                    return j_bg + jnp.sum(per_step)

                return jax.grad(cost_full)(x_iter)

            # Gauss-Newton outer iterations on the nonlinear cost.
            for _ in range(self.config.n_outer):
                # Build the observation operator J: x_0 → masked
                # trajectory observations (shape (T_plus_1, N)).
                def J_full(x_0):
                    trajectory = self._rollout(x_0, n_steps=T)

                    def _per_step(x_t, m_t):
                        return (
                            self.obs_op(x_t, mask=m_t)
                            if _accepts_mask(self.obs_op)
                            else self.obs_op(x_t)
                        ) * m_t

                    return jax.vmap(_per_step)(trajectory, mask_i)

                # GN Hessian as a hand-rolled mat-vec on the state
                # space (N,). Uses jax.linearize + jax.vjp to apply
                # H^T R^{-1} H v plus B^{-1} v without forming dense
                # matrices.
                _, jvp_fn = jax.linearize(J_full, x_b)
                _, vjp_fn = jax.vjp(J_full, x_b)

                def gn_hessian_matvec(v, _jvp_fn=jvp_fn, _vjp_fn=vjp_fn):
                    Hv = _jvp_fn(v)

                    # Apply per-time-step R^{-1}: vmap CG over time
                    def _r_inv(y):
                        return lx.linear_solve(
                            self.obs_cov_op,
                            y,
                            solver=lx.CG(atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-6),
                        ).value

                    R_inv_Hv = jax.vmap(_r_inv)(Hv)
                    (HtR_inv_H_v,) = _vjp_fn(R_inv_Hv)
                    B_inv_v = lx.linear_solve(
                        self.prior_cov_op,
                        v,
                        solver=lx.CG(atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-6),
                    ).value
                    return HtR_inv_H_v + B_inv_v

                gn_op = lx.FunctionLinearOperator(
                    gn_hessian_matvec,
                    jax.ShapeDtypeStruct(x_b.shape, x_b.dtype),
                    lx.positive_semidefinite_tag,
                )

                # RHS = -grad J(x_b)
                rhs = -cost_grad_for_outer(x_b)

                # Inner CG solve: GN_Hessian @ dx = rhs
                dx_star = lx.linear_solve(
                    gn_op,
                    rhs,
                    solver=lx.CG(
                        atol=self.config.cg_atol,
                        rtol=self.config.cg_rtol,
                        max_steps=self.config.n_inner,
                    ),
                ).value
                x_b = x_b + dx_star

            return x_b

        return jax.vmap(_one)(batch.input, batch.mask)

    def _analyse_points(self, batch: PointObsBatch, T: int) -> Float[Array, " N"]:
        r"""GN outer + CG inner on a point batch.

        With the whitened, padding-masked residual
        $r_i(x_0) = m_i (y_i - \mathcal H(M^{\tau_i}(x_0))(s_i)) / \sigma_i$,
        the cost is $\tfrac12 \lVert x_0 - x_b \rVert^2_{B^{-1}} +
        \tfrac12 \lVert r \rVert^2$ and the Gauss-Newton Hessian is
        $B^{-1} + r'^\top r'$.
        """
        obs_op = require_grid_point_obs(self.obs_op)

        def residual(x_0):
            preds = obs_op(self._rollout(x_0, n_steps=T), batch)
            return whitened_residual(preds, batch)

        def b_inv(v):
            return lx.linear_solve(
                self.prior_cov_op, v, solver=lx.CG(atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-6)
            ).value

        def cost_full(x_0):
            dx = x_0 - self.prior_mean
            return 0.5 * jnp.sum(dx * b_inv(dx)) + 0.5 * jnp.sum(residual(x_0) ** 2)

        x_b = self.prior_mean
        for _ in range(self.config.n_outer):
            _, jvp_fn = jax.linearize(residual, x_b)
            _, vjp_fn = jax.vjp(residual, x_b)

            def gn_hessian_matvec(v, _jvp_fn=jvp_fn, _vjp_fn=vjp_fn):
                (jt_j_v,) = _vjp_fn(_jvp_fn(v))
                return jt_j_v + b_inv(v)

            gn_op = lx.FunctionLinearOperator(
                gn_hessian_matvec,
                jax.ShapeDtypeStruct(x_b.shape, x_b.dtype),
                lx.positive_semidefinite_tag,
            )
            dx_star = lx.linear_solve(
                gn_op,
                -jax.grad(cost_full)(x_b),
                solver=lx.CG(
                    atol=self.config.cg_atol,
                    rtol=self.config.cg_rtol,
                    max_steps=self.config.n_inner,
                ),
            ).value
            x_b = x_b + dx_star
        return x_b

    def as_analysis_step(self) -> _IncrementalFourDVarAnalysisStep:
        return _IncrementalFourDVarAnalysisStep(self)

    class Incremental4DVar(eqx.Module):
    r"""Reduced-basis 4DVar.

    Attributes:
        forward: ``pipekit_cycle.ForwardModel`` supplying
            ``step(state, dt) -> state``.
        obs_op: Observation operator (linear or nonlinear). Supplies
            ``__call__`` and ``linearize``; ``__call__`` may accept a
            ``mask`` kwarg (`MaskedIdentity` / `InterpObs` style).
        prior_mean: Background $x_b$ of shape ``(N,)``.
        prior_cov_op: $B$. Used only when ``basis is None``.
        obs_cov_op: $R$.
        basis: Optional `ReducedBasis`. When supplied, the control is
            the coefficient vector ``X`` (shape ``(basis.nbasis,)``)
            and ``B^{-1}`` is replaced by ``basis.prior_inv`` — the same as
            ``parameterization=LinearParameterization(basis, prior_mean)``.
        parameterization: Optional
            [`StateParameterization`][vardax.StateParameterization]; the
            control is $\theta$, $x_0 = \psi(\theta)$ and
            $\mathrm{pen}(\theta)$ replaces the background term. Exclusive
            with ``basis``.
        minimiser: ``optimistix.AbstractMinimiser`` for the outer
            optimisation (default ``optx.BFGS(rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-6)``), or
            a [`Minimiser`][vardax.Minimiser] such as
            [`OptaxMinimiser`][vardax.OptaxMinimiser].
        minimiser_adjoint: ``optimistix.AbstractAdjoint`` for
            differentiating through the minimum. Default
            ``optx.ImplicitAdjoint``.
        max_steps: Iteration cap on the outer solver when ``minimiser``
            is an ``optimistix`` solver; a vardax `Minimiser` keeps its own.
    """

    forward: Any
    obs_op: Any
    prior_mean: Float[Array, " N"]
    prior_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator
    obs_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator
    basis: Any
    parameterization: StateParameterization | None
    minimiser: optx.AbstractMinimiser | Minimiser = eqx.field(static=True)
    minimiser_adjoint: optx.AbstractAdjoint = eqx.field(static=True)
    max_steps: int = eqx.field(static=True, default=200)

    def __init__(
        self,
        forward: Any,
        obs_op: Any,
        prior_mean: Float[Array, " N"],
        prior_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator,
        obs_cov_op: lx.AbstractLinearOperator,
        *,
        basis: Any = None,
        parameterization: StateParameterization | None = None,
        minimiser: optx.AbstractMinimiser | Minimiser | None = None,
        minimiser_adjoint: optx.AbstractAdjoint | None = None,
        max_steps: int = 200,
    ) -> None:
        self.forward = forward
        self.obs_op = obs_op
        self.prior_mean = prior_mean
        self.prior_cov_op = prior_cov_op
        self.obs_cov_op = obs_cov_op
        if basis is not None and parameterization is not None:
            raise ValueError(
                "Pass basis= or parameterization=, not both; "
                "LinearParameterization(basis, prior_mean) is the basis path."
            )
        self.basis = basis
        self.parameterization = parameterization
        self.minimiser = minimiser or optx.BFGS(rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-6)
        self.minimiser_adjoint = minimiser_adjoint or optx.ImplicitAdjoint()
        self.max_steps = max_steps

    def _rollout(
        self,
        x_0: Float[Array, " N"],
        n_steps: int,
    ) -> Float[Array, "T_plus_1 N"]:
        """Step the forward ``n_steps`` times, returning the ``T+1``-long trajectory."""
        dt = self.forward.dt

        def step_fn(x, _):
            x_new = self.forward.step(x, dt)
            return x_new, x_new

        _, trajectory = jax.lax.scan(step_fn, x_0, None, length=n_steps)
        return jnp.concatenate([x_0[None, :], trajectory], axis=0)

    def __call__(self, batch: Batch1D | PointObsBatch) -> Float[Array, "B N"]:
        """Reduced-basis 4DVar analysis: minimise over ``x_0`` (or ``X``).

        A [`PointObsBatch`][vardax.PointObsBatch] needs
        ``obs_op=GridPointObs(...)``: observation $i$ is compared with the
        trajectory state at ``time_index[i]`` over a window of ``n_times``
        states, with error variance $\\sigma_i^2$ (``obs_cov_op`` must
        be ``None`` or an identity, else ``ValueError``).
        """
        if isinstance(batch, PointObsBatch):
            check_point_obs_cov(self.obs_cov_op)
            n_steps = window_steps(batch)

            def _one_points(b: PointObsBatch) -> Float[Array, " N"]:
                def _obs_cost(
                    trajectory: Float[Array, "T_plus_1 N"],
                ) -> Float[Array, ""]:
                    return grid_point_obs_cost(self.obs_op, trajectory, b)

                return self._solve(_obs_cost, n_steps)

            return map_point_batch(_one_points, batch)

        T = batch.input.shape[1] - 1

        def _one(
            input_i: Float[Array, "T_plus_1 N"],
            mask_i: Float[Array, "T_plus_1 N"],
        ) -> Float[Array, " N"]:
            def _obs_cost(
                trajectory: Float[Array, "T_plus_1 N"],
            ) -> Float[Array, ""]:
                def _per_step(x_t, y_t, m_t):
                    y_pred = (
                        self.obs_op(x_t, mask=m_t)
                        if _accepts_mask(self.obs_op)
                        else self.obs_op(x_t)
                    )
                    residual = m_t * (y_t - y_pred)
                    # Solve against the marginalized covariance
                    # R~ = M R M + (I - M): for a 0/1 mask its inverse on
                    # the observed block equals (R_oo)^{-1}, so masked
                    # entries drop out of the likelihood exactly. Solving
                    # the full R against a zeroed residual would instead
                    # weight observed entries by the observed block of
                    # R^{-1}, biasing the analysis when R is correlated.
                    mask_op = lx.DiagonalLinearOperator(m_t)
                    r_masked = lx.TaggedLinearOperator(
                        mask_op @ self.obs_cov_op @ mask_op
                        + lx.DiagonalLinearOperator(1.0 - m_t),
                        lx.positive_semidefinite_tag,
                    )
                    R_inv_r = lx.linear_solve(
                        r_masked,
                        residual,
                        solver=lx.CG(atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-6),
                    ).value
                    return 0.5 * jnp.sum(residual * R_inv_r)

                per_step_costs = jax.vmap(_per_step)(trajectory, input_i, mask_i)
                return jnp.sum(per_step_costs)

            return self._solve(_obs_cost, T)

        return jax.vmap(_one)(batch.input, batch.mask)

    def _solve(self, _obs_cost: Callable[[Array], Array], T: int) -> Float[Array, " N"]:
        """Minimise background (or penalty) plus the trajectory ``_obs_cost``."""
        param = self.parameterization
        if self.basis is not None:
            # The reduced-basis path, unchanged; it equals
            # LinearParameterization(basis, prior_mean) mathematically.
            def cost(X: Float[Array, " M"], _args: Any) -> Float[Array, ""]:
                j_bg = 0.5 * jnp.sum(X * self.basis.prior_inv(X))
                x_0 = self.prior_mean + self.basis.operg(0.0, X).reshape(
                    self.prior_mean.shape
                )
                return j_bg + _obs_cost(self._rollout(x_0, n_steps=T))

            y0 = jnp.zeros((self.basis.nbasis,), dtype=self.prior_mean.dtype)
        elif param is not None:

            def cost(theta: Any, _args: Any) -> Float[Array, ""]:
                x_0 = param.decode(theta).reshape(self.prior_mean.shape)
                return param.penalty(theta) + _obs_cost(self._rollout(x_0, n_steps=T))

            y0 = param.init_control()
        else:

            def cost(x_0: Float[Array, " N"], _args: Any) -> Float[Array, ""]:
                dx = x_0 - self.prior_mean
                B_inv_dx = lx.linear_solve(
                    self.prior_cov_op,
                    dx,
                    solver=lx.CG(atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-6),
                ).value
                j_bg = 0.5 * jnp.sum(dx * B_inv_dx)
                return j_bg + _obs_cost(self._rollout(x_0, n_steps=T))

            y0 = self.prior_mean

        x_star = minimise(
            self.minimiser,
            cost,
            y0,
            adjoint=self.minimiser_adjoint,
            max_steps=self.max_steps,
        )
        if self.basis is not None:
            return self.prior_mean + self.basis.operg(0.0, x_star).reshape(
                self.prior_mean.shape
            )
        if param is not None:
            return param.decode(x_star).reshape(self.prior_mean.shape)
        return x_star

    def as_analysis_step(self) -> _Incremental4DVarAnalysisStep:
        """Adapt to ``pipekit_cycle.AnalysisStep`` (Decision D8)."""
        return _Incremental4DVarAnalysisStep(self)

    Neural-field 4DVar¶

    SpaceTimeFieldVar fits one continuous field \(u(t, s) = f_\theta(t, s)\) over the whole window to point observations, with an optional PDE residual as a soft constraint and weight decay in place of \(B\); no rollout. It returns a SpaceTimeFieldResult, queryable anywhere, and ensemble(...) gives a deep-ensemble spread.

    vardax — Modular variational data assimilation with learned components.

    All public symbols are re-exported from the private _src subpackage so that user code imports from the top-level namespace:

    import vardax

model = vardax.FourDVarNet1D(...)

    SpaceTimeFieldVar ¶

    Bases: Module

    Neural-field 4D-Var: fit one continuous field \(u(t, s) = f_\theta(t, s)\).

    Minimises, over the network weights \(\theta\),

    \[ J(\theta) = \tfrac{1}{2}\sum_k m_k \frac{\big(y_k - f_\theta(t_k, s_k) \big)^2}{\sigma_k^2} + \frac{\lambda}{2 N_c}\sum_j \big\lVert \mathcal N[f_\theta](c_j) \big\rVert^2 + \frac{\alpha}{2}\lVert\theta\rVert^2 , \]

    with the observations of a PointObsBatch (\(m_k = 0\) on padding rows, which contribute nothing, NaN included), the physics term of an optional ResidualPenalty and weight decay \(\alpha\). There is no background covariance and no rollout: the whole window is the field, which can be queried and differentiated anywhere (Oh 2025).

    Coordinates put time first: the field maps a point (t, *s) of shape (1 + D,) to (K,) (or a scalar), the observation coordinates are (N_obs, 1 + D) in the same order, and so are the collocation points, as the residuals of vardax.examples expect. The observed quantity is the field's single output (FieldPointObs); a multi-channel field needs its own wrapper.

    Scale of \(\lambda\): the observation term is a sum over the \(N_\text{obs}\) valid observations, each weighted by \(1/\sigma_k^2\), while the residual term is a mean over the collocation points. A unit change of the field everywhere moves the first by about \(N_\text{obs}/(2\sigma^2)\) and the second by about \(\lambda/2\) times the squared residual it causes, so \(\lambda\) trades off against \(N_\text{obs}/(2\sigma^2)\) and must grow with it to keep the same balance (the advection test uses \(\lambda = 10^3\) for 100 observations with \(\sigma = 0.05\), where \(N_\text{obs}/(2\sigma^2) = 2 \times 10^4\)).

    The fit runs in one eqx.filter_jit-compiled function of the model, the observations and the key, so repeated analyses with new observations (or a new weight_decay or penalty weight, both array leaves) of the same shapes do not recompile.

    The penalty's collocation points are fixed during a fit: a ResidualPenalty with a sampler draws them once, from key, at the start of the analysis, so the cost the minimiser sees is deterministic (its patience test, best-iterate tracking and implicit adjoint all assume that). Draw more points, or refit with new keys, for a better estimate of the expected residual.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    field Any

    The initial network, a single-example eqx.Module (1 + D,) -> (K,) such as geonnax.SIREN or geonnax.NeuralFieldMLP. Its parameters are the initial control.
    residual ResidualPenalty | None

    Optional ResidualPenalty (the physics term); None fits the observations alone.
    weight_decay Float[Array, '']

    \(\alpha \ge 0\), stored as a 0-d array (a leaf: it can be changed without recompiling and differentiated).
    minimiser OptaxMinimiser | OptimistixMinimiser

    An OptaxMinimiser (the default, Adam with learning rate \(10^{-3}\)) or an OptimistixMinimiser.
    filter_spec Any

    Which leaves of field are the control, as in NeuralFieldParameterization: exclude frozen arrays (random Fourier frequencies) so the weight decay does not shrink them. Default eqx.is_inexact_array.
    t0 float

    Start of the window, \(t_0\) (default 0.0).

    Examples:

    A field linear in fixed features, \(f_w(t, x) = w_0 + w_1 x\), with no physics is Bayesian linear regression: the analysis is the ridge solution, here \(w^\star = (0, 1)\) to within the small weight decay.

    >>> import equinox as eqx, jax, jax.numpy as jnp, vardax
>>> class Line(eqx.Module):
...     w: jax.Array
...
...     def __call__(self, s):
...         return (self.w[0] + self.w[1] * s[1])[None]
>>> obs = vardax.PointObsBatch(
...     coords=jnp.array([[0.0, -1.0], [0.5, 0.0], [1.0, 1.0], [0.0, 9.0]]),
...     values=jnp.array([-1.0, 0.0, 1.0, jnp.nan]),  # last row: padding
...     sigma=jnp.ones(4),
...     valid=jnp.array([True, True, True, False]),
... )
>>> ana = vardax.SpaceTimeFieldVar(
...     field=Line(jnp.zeros(2)),
...     weight_decay=1e-6,
...     minimiser=vardax.OptimistixMinimiser(),
... )
>>> result = ana(obs)
>>> result.initial_condition(jnp.array([[0.5], [2.0]])).round(3)
Array([0.5, 2. ], dtype=float32)

    class SpaceTimeFieldVar(eqx.Module):
    r"""Neural-field 4D-Var: fit one continuous field $u(t, s) = f_\theta(t, s)$.

    Minimises, over the network weights $\theta$,

    $$
    J(\theta) = \tfrac{1}{2}\sum_k m_k \frac{\big(y_k - f_\theta(t_k, s_k)
        \big)^2}{\sigma_k^2}
      + \frac{\lambda}{2 N_c}\sum_j \big\lVert \mathcal N[f_\theta](c_j)
        \big\rVert^2
      + \frac{\alpha}{2}\lVert\theta\rVert^2 ,
    $$

    with the observations of a [`PointObsBatch`][vardax.PointObsBatch]
    ($m_k = 0$ on padding rows, which contribute nothing, ``NaN``
    included), the physics term of an optional
    [`ResidualPenalty`][vardax.ResidualPenalty] and weight decay $\alpha$.
    There is no background covariance and no rollout: the whole window
    is the field, which can be queried and differentiated anywhere
    (Oh 2025).

    Coordinates put **time first**: the field maps a point
    ``(t, *s)`` of shape ``(1 + D,)`` to ``(K,)`` (or a scalar), the
    observation coordinates are ``(N_obs, 1 + D)`` in the same order, and
    so are the collocation points, as the residuals of
    `vardax.examples` expect. The observed quantity is the field's single
    output (`FieldPointObs`); a multi-channel field needs its own wrapper.

    Scale of $\lambda$: the observation term is a *sum* over the
    $N_\text{obs}$ valid observations, each weighted by $1/\sigma_k^2$,
    while the residual term is a *mean* over the collocation points. A
    unit change of the field everywhere moves the first by about
    $N_\text{obs}/(2\sigma^2)$ and the second by about $\lambda/2$ times
    the squared residual it causes, so $\lambda$ trades off against
    $N_\text{obs}/(2\sigma^2)$ and must grow with it to keep the same
    balance (the advection test uses $\lambda = 10^3$ for 100
    observations with $\sigma = 0.05$, where
    $N_\text{obs}/(2\sigma^2) = 2 \times 10^4$).

    The fit runs in one ``eqx.filter_jit``-compiled function of the model,
    the observations and the key, so repeated analyses with new
    observations (or a new ``weight_decay`` or penalty weight, both array
    leaves) of the same shapes do not recompile.

    The penalty's collocation points are fixed during a fit: a
    ``ResidualPenalty`` with a ``sampler`` draws them once, from ``key``,
    at the start of the analysis, so the cost the minimiser sees is
    deterministic (its patience test, best-iterate tracking and implicit
    adjoint all assume that). Draw more points, or refit with new keys,
    for a better estimate of the expected residual.

    Attributes:
        field: The initial network, a single-example ``eqx.Module``
            ``(1 + D,) -> (K,)`` such as `geonnax.SIREN` or
            `geonnax.NeuralFieldMLP`. Its parameters are the initial
            control.
        residual: Optional [`ResidualPenalty`][vardax.ResidualPenalty]
            (the physics term); ``None`` fits the observations alone.
        weight_decay: $\alpha \ge 0$, stored as a 0-d array (a leaf: it
            can be changed without recompiling and differentiated).
        minimiser: An [`OptaxMinimiser`][vardax.OptaxMinimiser] (the
            default, Adam with learning rate $10^{-3}$) or an
            [`OptimistixMinimiser`][vardax.OptimistixMinimiser].
        filter_spec: Which leaves of ``field`` are the control, as in
            [`NeuralFieldParameterization`][vardax.NeuralFieldParameterization]:
            exclude frozen arrays (random Fourier frequencies) so the weight
            decay does not shrink them. Default ``eqx.is_inexact_array``.
        t0: Start of the window, $t_0$ (default ``0.0``).

    Examples:
        A field linear in fixed features, $f_w(t, x) = w_0 + w_1 x$, with no
        physics is Bayesian linear regression: the analysis is the ridge
        solution, here $w^\star = (0, 1)$ to within the small weight decay.

        >>> import equinox as eqx, jax, jax.numpy as jnp, vardax
        >>> class Line(eqx.Module):
        ...     w: jax.Array
        ...
        ...     def __call__(self, s):
        ...         return (self.w[0] + self.w[1] * s[1])[None]
        >>> obs = vardax.PointObsBatch(
        ...     coords=jnp.array([[0.0, -1.0], [0.5, 0.0], [1.0, 1.0], [0.0, 9.0]]),
        ...     values=jnp.array([-1.0, 0.0, 1.0, jnp.nan]),  # last row: padding
        ...     sigma=jnp.ones(4),
        ...     valid=jnp.array([True, True, True, False]),
        ... )
        >>> ana = vardax.SpaceTimeFieldVar(
        ...     field=Line(jnp.zeros(2)),
        ...     weight_decay=1e-6,
        ...     minimiser=vardax.OptimistixMinimiser(),
        ... )
        >>> result = ana(obs)
        >>> result.initial_condition(jnp.array([[0.5], [2.0]])).round(3)
        Array([0.5, 2. ], dtype=float32)

    References:
        Oh, Y. (2025). On the effect of neural field reparameterization for
        4DVAR. arXiv:2509.21751.
    """

    field: Any
    residual: ResidualPenalty | None
    weight_decay: Float[Array, ""] = eqx.field(converter=jnp.asarray)
    minimiser: OptaxMinimiser | OptimistixMinimiser = eqx.field(static=True)
    filter_spec: Any = eqx.field(static=True)
    t0: float = eqx.field(static=True)

    def __init__(
        self,
        field: Any,
        residual: ResidualPenalty | None = None,
        weight_decay: float | Float[Array, ""] = 0.0,
        minimiser: OptaxMinimiser | OptimistixMinimiser | None = None,
        *,
        filter_spec: Any = eqx.is_inexact_array,
        t0: float = 0.0,
    ) -> None:
        if jnp.ndim(weight_decay) != 0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"weight_decay must be a scalar; got shape {jnp.shape(weight_decay)}."
            )
        try:
            negative = float(weight_decay) < 0
        except jax.errors.ConcretizationTypeError:
            negative = False  # built under a transform: the sign is not known
        if negative:
            raise ValueError(f"weight_decay must be >= 0, got {weight_decay}.")
        if residual is not None and not isinstance(residual, ResidualPenalty):
            raise TypeError(
                "residual must be a vardax.ResidualPenalty or None; got "
                f"{type(residual).__name__}."
            )
        if minimiser is None:
            minimiser = OptaxMinimiser()
        if not isinstance(minimiser, OptaxMinimiser | OptimistixMinimiser):
            raise TypeError(
                "minimiser must be a vardax.OptaxMinimiser or "
                f"vardax.OptimistixMinimiser; got {type(minimiser).__name__}."
            )
        self.field = field
        self.residual = residual
        self.weight_decay = weight_decay
        self.minimiser = minimiser
        self.filter_spec = filter_spec
        self.t0 = t0

    @property
    def _parameterization(self) -> NeuralFieldParameterization:
        # Only the control split, `as_field` and the penalty are used: the
        # space-time field is evaluated at the observation and collocation
        # points, never on a grid, so the grid is empty. The weight is 1
        # (penalty ½‖θ‖²): alpha multiplies it in the cost, as an array leaf.
        return NeuralFieldParameterization(
            self.field,
            jnp.zeros((0, 1)),
            1.0,
            filter_spec=self.filter_spec,
        )

    def _fixed_residual(self, key: PRNGKeyArray | None) -> ResidualPenalty | None:
        """The residual penalty with its collocation points drawn and fixed."""
        residual = self.residual
        if residual is None or residual.sampler is None:
            return residual
        if key is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "The residual penalty has a sampler: pass key= to draw its "
                "collocation points."
            )
        return ResidualPenalty(
            residual_fn=residual.residual_fn,
            collocation=residual.sampler(key),
            weight=residual.weight,
        )

    def __call__(
        self, obs: PointObsBatch, *, key: PRNGKeyArray | None = None
    ) -> SpaceTimeFieldResult:
        """Fit the field to one sample of point observations.

        Args:
            obs: The observations, one sample (``values`` of shape
                ``(N_obs,)``, ``coords`` ``(N_obs, 1 + D)`` with time first;
                ``time_index`` and ``n_times`` are not used). For a batch
                of samples, ``eqx.filter_vmap`` over this call.
            key: Draws the collocation points when the residual penalty
                has a ``sampler``; unused otherwise.

        Returns:
            A [`SpaceTimeFieldResult`][vardax.SpaceTimeFieldResult].

        Raises:
            TypeError: If ``obs`` is not a `PointObsBatch`.
            ValueError: If ``obs`` carries a batch axis, or the penalty
                needs a key and none is given.
        """
        if not isinstance(obs, PointObsBatch):
            raise TypeError(
                f"obs must be a vardax.PointObsBatch; got {type(obs).__name__}."
            )
        if obs.values.ndim != 1:
            raise ValueError(
                "SpaceTimeFieldVar fits one sample: obs.values must be "
                f"(N_obs,), got shape {obs.values.shape}; use eqx.filter_vmap "
                "for a batch."
            )
        return _fit(self, obs, key)

    def ensemble(
        self,
        obs: PointObsBatch,
        field_init: Any,
        n_members: int,
        *,
        key: PRNGKeyArray,
    ) -> SpaceTimeFieldResult:
        r"""A deep ensemble: refit from ``n_members`` random initialisations.

        Each member re-initialises the field with ``field_init`` and draws
        its own collocation points (when the penalty has a sampler), then
        fits as `__call__` does; the members run under ``eqx.filter_vmap``.
        The spread of the members is a heuristic uncertainty: small where
        the observations pin the field down, large away from them. A
        $\theta$-space Laplace push-forward $J \Sigma_\theta J^\top$
        ($J = \partial u / \partial\theta$) is not implemented.

        Args:
            obs: The observations, one sample.
            field_init: ``key -> field``, building a network with the
                same structure as ``self.field`` (e.g.
                ``lambda k: geonnax.SIREN.init(2, 32, 1, depth=3, key=k)``).
            n_members: Number of members, at least 1.
            key: Split into one initialisation key and one collocation key
                per member.

        Returns:
            A [`SpaceTimeFieldResult`][vardax.SpaceTimeFieldResult] whose
            array leaves carry a leading axis of size ``n_members``.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If ``n_members < 1``.
        """
        if n_members < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"n_members must be >= 1, got {n_members}.")

        def member(k: PRNGKeyArray) -> SpaceTimeFieldResult:
            k_init, k_colloc = jax.random.split(k)
            model = eqx.tree_at(lambda m: m.field, self, field_init(k_init))
            return model(obs, key=k_colloc)

        return eqx.filter_vmap(member)(jax.random.split(key, n_members))

    def as_analysis_step(
        self,
        grid: Float[Array, "N D"] | None = None,
        *,
        key: PRNGKeyArray | None = None,
    ) -> _SpaceTimeFieldAnalysisStep:
        r"""Adapt to ``pipekit_cycle.AnalysisStep``.

        The step fits the field to the cycle's observations. With a
        ``grid`` it returns the analysis at the window start on it,
        $u(t_0, s_j)$ (`SpaceTimeFieldResult.initial_condition`), the
        state a ``ForwardModel`` steps on; without one it returns the
        [`SpaceTimeFieldResult`][vardax.SpaceTimeFieldResult] itself.

        The collocation points are drawn **once**, here, from ``key``,
        and reused by every cycle. ``pipekit_cycle.DACycle`` passes no
        time: the times are the first column of each cycle's
        ``PointObsBatch``, so they must be **window-relative**, in the
        same window $[t_0, t_1]$ every cycle as the collocation points.
        The step checks that (when the times are concrete): $t_0$ and the
        valid observation times must lie in the collocation points' time
        range, widened by 10 % on each side for the gaps a random draw
        leaves at the ends.

        Args:
            grid: Spatial points $s_j$ of the returned state, ``(N, D)``,
                or ``None``.
            key: Collocation key; required when the penalty has a
                ``sampler``.

        Returns:
            The adapter.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If ``grid`` is not 2-D, the penalty has a sampler
                and ``key`` is ``None``, or $t_0$ is outside the
                collocation window.
        """
        if grid is not None:
            grid = jnp.asarray(grid)
            if grid.ndim != 2:
                raise ValueError(f"grid must be 2-D (N, D); got shape {grid.shape}.")
        if self.residual is not None and self.residual.sampler is not None:
            if key is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    "The residual penalty has a sampler: pass key= to "
                    "as_analysis_step to draw the collocation points, which "
                    "every cycle then reuses."
                )
        model = eqx.tree_at(
            lambda m: m.residual,
            self,
            self._fixed_residual(key),
            is_leaf=lambda x: x is None,
        )
        window = _collocation_window(model.residual)
        if window is not None and not window[0] <= self.t0 <= window[1]:
            raise ValueError(
                f"t0 = {self.t0} is outside the collocation time window "
                f"[{window[0]:.4g}, {window[1]:.4g}]: the initial condition "
                "would be unconstrained by the physics."
            )
        return _SpaceTimeFieldAnalysisStep(model, grid)

    def ensemble(
    self,
    obs: PointObsBatch,
    field_init: Any,
    n_members: int,
    *,
    key: PRNGKeyArray,
) -> SpaceTimeFieldResult:
    r"""A deep ensemble: refit from ``n_members`` random initialisations.

    Each member re-initialises the field with ``field_init`` and draws
    its own collocation points (when the penalty has a sampler), then
    fits as `__call__` does; the members run under ``eqx.filter_vmap``.
    The spread of the members is a heuristic uncertainty: small where
    the observations pin the field down, large away from them. A
    $\theta$-space Laplace push-forward $J \Sigma_\theta J^\top$
    ($J = \partial u / \partial\theta$) is not implemented.

    Args:
        obs: The observations, one sample.
        field_init: ``key -> field``, building a network with the
            same structure as ``self.field`` (e.g.
            ``lambda k: geonnax.SIREN.init(2, 32, 1, depth=3, key=k)``).
        n_members: Number of members, at least 1.
        key: Split into one initialisation key and one collocation key
            per member.

    Returns:
        A [`SpaceTimeFieldResult`][vardax.SpaceTimeFieldResult] whose
        array leaves carry a leading axis of size ``n_members``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``n_members < 1``.
    """
    if n_members < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"n_members must be >= 1, got {n_members}.")

    def member(k: PRNGKeyArray) -> SpaceTimeFieldResult:
        k_init, k_colloc = jax.random.split(k)
        model = eqx.tree_at(lambda m: m.field, self, field_init(k_init))
        return model(obs, key=k_colloc)

    return eqx.filter_vmap(member)(jax.random.split(key, n_members))

    def as_analysis_step(
    self,
    grid: Float[Array, "N D"] | None = None,
    *,
    key: PRNGKeyArray | None = None,
) -> _SpaceTimeFieldAnalysisStep:
    r"""Adapt to ``pipekit_cycle.AnalysisStep``.

    The step fits the field to the cycle's observations. With a
    ``grid`` it returns the analysis at the window start on it,
    $u(t_0, s_j)$ (`SpaceTimeFieldResult.initial_condition`), the
    state a ``ForwardModel`` steps on; without one it returns the
    [`SpaceTimeFieldResult`][vardax.SpaceTimeFieldResult] itself.

    The collocation points are drawn **once**, here, from ``key``,
    and reused by every cycle. ``pipekit_cycle.DACycle`` passes no
    time: the times are the first column of each cycle's
    ``PointObsBatch``, so they must be **window-relative**, in the
    same window $[t_0, t_1]$ every cycle as the collocation points.
    The step checks that (when the times are concrete): $t_0$ and the
    valid observation times must lie in the collocation points' time
    range, widened by 10 % on each side for the gaps a random draw
    leaves at the ends.

    Args:
        grid: Spatial points $s_j$ of the returned state, ``(N, D)``,
            or ``None``.
        key: Collocation key; required when the penalty has a
            ``sampler``.

    Returns:
        The adapter.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``grid`` is not 2-D, the penalty has a sampler
            and ``key`` is ``None``, or $t_0$ is outside the
            collocation window.
    """
    if grid is not None:
        grid = jnp.asarray(grid)
        if grid.ndim != 2:
            raise ValueError(f"grid must be 2-D (N, D); got shape {grid.shape}.")
    if self.residual is not None and self.residual.sampler is not None:
        if key is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "The residual penalty has a sampler: pass key= to "
                "as_analysis_step to draw the collocation points, which "
                "every cycle then reuses."
            )
    model = eqx.tree_at(
        lambda m: m.residual,
        self,
        self._fixed_residual(key),
        is_leaf=lambda x: x is None,
    )
    window = _collocation_window(model.residual)
    if window is not None and not window[0] <= self.t0 <= window[1]:
        raise ValueError(
            f"t0 = {self.t0} is outside the collocation time window "
            f"[{window[0]:.4g}, {window[1]:.4g}]: the initial condition "
            "would be unconstrained by the physics."
        )
    return _SpaceTimeFieldAnalysisStep(model, grid)

    class SpaceTimeFieldResult(eqx.Module):
    r"""A fitted space-time field and its minimisation diagnostics.

    Attributes:
        field: The analysis $f_{\theta^\star}$, a single-example callable
            of one space-time point ``(t, *s)`` of shape ``(1 + D,)``.
        t0: Start of the window, $t_0$, used by `initial_condition`.
        cost: $J(\theta^\star)$.
        grad_norm: $\lVert\nabla J(\theta^\star)\rVert_2$; a first-order
            optimiser stopped by its step budget leaves it non-zero.
        num_steps: Optimiser steps taken.

    An [`ensemble`][vardax.SpaceTimeFieldVar.ensemble] returns one result
    whose array leaves carry a leading member axis; evaluate it with
    ``eqx.filter_vmap(lambda r: r.initial_condition(grid))(result)``.
    """

    field: Any
    t0: float = eqx.field(static=True)
    cost: Float[Array, ""]
    grad_norm: Float[Array, ""]
    num_steps: Int[Array, ""]

    def evaluate(self, coords: Float[Array, "N P"]) -> Float[Array, "N ..."]:
        """Evaluate the field at space-time points.

        Args:
            coords: Points ``(t, *s)``, shape ``(N, 1 + D)``.

        Returns:
            ``(N,)`` for a single-channel field, else ``(N, K)``.
        """
        return _evaluate(self.field, jnp.asarray(coords))

    def initial_condition(self, grid: Float[Array, "N D"]) -> Float[Array, "N ..."]:
        r"""The analysis at the window start, $u(t_0, s_j)$, on a grid.

        This is the initial state for a forecast with a ``ForwardModel``.

        Args:
            grid: Spatial points $s_j$, shape ``(N, D)``.

        Returns:
            ``(N,)`` for a single-channel field, else ``(N, K)``.
        """
        grid = jnp.asarray(grid)
        if grid.ndim != 2:
            raise ValueError(f"grid must be 2-D (N, D); got shape {grid.shape}.")
        if not jnp.issubdtype(grid.dtype, jnp.inexact):
            # An integer grid would truncate t0 in the time column.
            grid = grid.astype(jnp.result_type(float))
        time = jnp.full((grid.shape[0], 1), self.t0, dtype=grid.dtype)
        return _evaluate(self.field, jnp.concatenate([time, grid], axis=-1))

    Learned solvers — 4DVarNet¶

    End-to-end-trainable 4DVar: the variational cost is kept explicit, but the inner-loop descent direction is produced by a ConvLSTM gradient modulator instead of a hand-tuned optimiser. The 1D variant operates on Batch1D (e.g. Lorenz-96 trajectories); the 2D variant on Batch2D / Batch2DMultivar fields (e.g. SSH reconstruction). The inner-loop iteration functions live on the Costs, Priors & Solvers page; training utilities on Training & Adjoints.

    vardax — Modular variational data assimilation with learned components.

    All public symbols are re-exported from the private _src subpackage so that user code imports from the top-level namespace:

    import vardax

model = vardax.FourDVarNet1D(...)
